newsitem.title: JAPAN: Asian crude market shrugs off Iraqi cancellation.
newsitem.headline: Asian crude market shrugs off Iraqi cancellation.

text.p: The Asian oil market remained relaxed on Thursday despite news that Iraq had cancelled a deal to sell Basrah Light crude to Japan's leading oil refiner Nippon Oil Co Ltd at the last minute.
A Nippon Oil spokesman confirmed that Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organization (SOMO) had cancelled a 900,000-barrel cargo that had been due to be loaded at the end of May.

Sources close to the United Nations in New York said on Wednesday that Iraq had cancelled two shipments -- one for Nippon Oil and a 1.3 million-barrel cargo purchased by Bayoil of the United States due to load in early June.
Iraq notified Nippon Oil of the cancellation on Wednesday, but no explanation for the move was given, the Nippon Oil spokesman said.
Asked whether they planned to appeal to the U.N., the spokesman said the company had no plans to do so.
"We believe it's a final decision (by Iraq)," he said.

Bayoil on Wednesday won U.N. approval to proceed with loading its Iraqi crude oil despite the cancellation, although it was unclear if the firm would be allowed to load the entire 1.3 million barrels.

News of the cancellation failed to excite the market, and there were some uncomfirmed reports that Nippon Oil had already purchased 900,000 barrels of Saudi Arabia's Arab Light to replace the cancelled Basrah Light cargo.
The deal could not be immediately confirmed.
One trader with a refiner said the Arab Light cargo had been purchased directly from Saudi Arabia at the official selling price.

Other traders said that even if Nippon Oil had failed to make a fresh purchase to replace the Basrah Light, the news was unlikely to have an impact on the physical market, which is currently trading July-loading cargoes of Middle East crudes.
A second trader said that most Japanese oil companies had stocks worth about 70 days of crude oil, and that the cancellation of one cargo was unlikely to make bearish market sentiment better.
Nippon Oil has already imported 1.1 million barrels of Basrah Light at the end of February.
The cancelled 900,000 barrel cargo was to have been Nippon Oil's second Iraqi crude oil cargo.
Japan was importing roughly 200,000 barrels-per-day of crude oil from Iraq before sanctions were imposed against Iraq for its invasion of Kuwait in 1990.
Iraq's current U.N. sponsored oil-for-food deal expires on June 7, and the U.N. Security Council is expected to decide next week whether to renew the contract and on what terms.
